text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- Parliament drops a censure motion aimed at toppling the Islamist-led government. Islamist and secularist MPs brawl while the main opposition party leader is giving his speech.
- Former health minister Yildirim Aktuna, who voted for a censure motion to topple the coalition, says he would resign from his conservative True Path Party.
MILLIYET
- Gunmen attack a new building of the private television channel ATV.
- Turkey's reported acceptance of European Union quotas on agricultural products, milk and meat opens the way for Europe to manipulate the Turkish agriculture and breeding sectors.
HURRIYET

- Conservative coalition partner Tansu Ciller convinces party dissidents to vote against the government censure motion by swearing on the holy Koran she would break up the government if she does not become prime minister within two weeks.
- Non-governmental organisations, trade unions and other civilian groups representing some 30 million people unite against the Islamist-led government.
YENI YUZYIL
- Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan says there will be no early elections before the year 2000.
- Fugitive Cypriot tycoon Asil Nadir returns to Turkey to invest in the media, tourism and food sectors.
RADIKAL
- Interior Minister Meral Aksener sends a decree limiting the authority of police chief Alaaddin Yuksel, who was re-appointed by a court decision after being ousted by Aksener.
- Constitutional court annuls an article allowing the sale of state-owned properties under the control of a state pension fund.
DUNYA
- The public social security organisation is to allow private banks to pay out pensions in a bid to shorten long queues at state-owned banks.
ZAMAN
- The Turkish armed forces have killed 1,088 Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerrillas in a seven-day-old incursion into northern Iraq.
